items.title: 68191_William (Bill) H. Challis Oral History Interview
items.q: Anyway, I got in touch with Willard. He was working with Shilkret on different things. Shilkret at that time had five radio accounts...

ctx.x: you don't even hear him. You know, they just ran roughshod over some of the things that we had that we could do. Later on we did 'My Pretty Girl' and it was liked by the musicians, which, I guess, that's what we were trying to satisfy and we were trying to make something that would impress the musicians.

The dance public in those days, anyway, it was a different dance public. It wasn't like the kind that would go into the Paramount and clap and scream like Benny Goodman had, which came along with swing. This was the old jazz and to try to impress them you had to things like the slide whistle and some of the tricks that Whiteman had, he had it made and besides they got all good tunes, and besides Shilkret got all the other good tunes. And Roger Kahn got the 'Blue Room' to do. We would have liked to have done Blue…

Tommy Gott, Arnold Brilhant, Alfie Alphie Evans and Joe and Eddie. He had a real crackerjack band. We used to go over and listen to it. But these were angles that we couldn't seem to get by. So we went back to Detroit and let's say with out tail between our legs, but we were pretty sure -- waiting for the tunes to come out, nothing happened, but 'Sunday' gave us a little kick, but that was the only one.
